title: Cruise-linked Andes virus and severe hantavirus lung disease: A narrative review

analysis.scope_and_question: The 2026 cruise-linked Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak represents a rare but high-consequence travel-associated zoonotic event, combining likely land-based acquisition before embarkation, limited onboard human-to-human transmission, delayed clinical recognition, and multinational public health coordination.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the outbreak, ANDV biology, transmission dynamics, clinical presentation, diagnostics, management, and implications for maritime and expedition travel medicine.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: As of 2 July 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) had reported 13 cases linked to the motor vessel (M/V) Hondius outbreak, including 12 laboratory-confirmed infections, one probable case, and three deaths.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Available evidence supports likely land-based acquisition before embarkation followed by limited onboard human-to-human transmission, without sustained spread.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The outbreak highlights critical preparedness gaps in shipboard triage, contact tracing, specimen transport, genomic surveillance, risk communication, and cross-border follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: The 2026 cruise-linked Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak represents a rare but high-consequence travel-associated zoonotic event, combining likely land-based acquisition before embarkation, limited onboard human-to-human transmission, delayed clinical recognition, and multinational public health coordination. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the outbreak, ANDV biology, transmission dynamics, clinical presentation, diagnostics, management, and implications for maritime and expedition travel medicine. As of 2 July 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) had reported 13 cases linked to the motor vessel (M/V) Hondius outbreak, including 12 laboratory-confirmed infections, one probable case, and three deaths. Available evidence supports likely land-based acquisition before embarkation followed by limited onboard human-to-human transmission, without sustained spread. The outbreak highlights critical preparedness gaps in shipboard triage, contact tracing, specimen transport, genomic surveillance, risk communication, and cross-border follow-up.

title: Neurological Manifestations of Hantavirus Infection: A Review.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines neurological manifestations of hantavirus infection, focusing on disease syndromes, host transmission routes, and the central question of how hantaviruses cause neurological complications in humans [A1, A2, A3].
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review summarizing documented neurological complications of hantavirus infection without specifying databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria [A13].
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Hantavirus infections primarily cause pulmonary syndrome with high mortality or hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome; neurological involvement is typically secondary to hypoxic, ischemic, or metabolic injury [A4, A5, A6, A7]. Neurological complications may include meningoencephalitis, pituitary apoplexy, seizures, myelitis, and peripheral neuropathy, though these are rare [A8, A9].
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The pathophysiology of neurological manifestations remains poorly understood, and there is a lack of prospective studies or experimental models to characterize these complications [A3, A13]. No specific antiviral therapies are approved, and preclinical efficacy has not translated into clinical practice [A10].
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Research priorities include prospective studies and experimental models to elucidate mechanisms, identify therapeutic targets, and develop management guidelines for neurological hantavirus complications [A13]. Clinical management currently relies on supportive care and symptom treatment [A11].

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates neurological manifestations of hantavirus infection, highlighting two primary disease syndromes: pulmonary syndrome with high mortality and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome. Neurological complications, though uncommon, include meningoencephalitis, pituitary apoplexy, seizures, myelitis, and peripheral neuropathy, typically arising from secondary hypoxic, ischemic, or metabolic injury. The review underscores significant gaps in understanding pathophysiology and the absence of approved antiviral therapies, despite preclinical efficacy. Management remains supportive, emphasizing the need for prospective studies and experimental models to clarify mechanisms, identify therapeutic targets, and establish clinical guidelines.

title: First nationwide full-genome characterisation of human-derived Andes virus in Chile: a retrospective genomic epidemiology study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Andes virus (ANDV) is the only hantavirus known to transmit between humans and causes hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in Chile and Argentina.

analysis.methods: Consensus sequences for the S, M, and L segments were generated, and genetic clustering and divergence were assessed using phylogenetic inference and variant calling.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The identification of geographically structured variants indicates that ANDV diversity in Chile is driven by regional diversification rather than clinical outcome.

analysis.summary_en: Andes virus (ANDV) is the only hantavirus known to transmit between humans and causes hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in Chile and Argentina. Clinical samples from patients with confirmed ANDV, collected between March 9, 2011, and June 27, 2024, were analysed and sequenced. Consensus sequences for the S, M, and L segments were generated, and genetic clustering and divergence were assessed using phylogenetic inference and variant calling. We analysed clinical samples from 58 infected individuals and identified two major genomic variants of ANDV with distinct geographical distributions, defined by regionally structured patterns of nucleotide and amino acid substitutions across the S, M, and L segments: ANDV Chi-North (central Chile) and ANDV-South (southern Chile). The identification of geographically structured variants indicates that ANDV diversity in Chile is driven by regional diversification rather than clinical outcome. These findings refine current understanding of ANDV evolution and highlight the need for continued integrated genomic surveillance in endemic regions. title: Ecological Cascades and Future Hantavirus Spillover Risk in a Changing Climate

analysis.research_question_and_background: The 2026 multi-country cruise ship outbreak of Andes virus highlights the unpredictable and globalized threat posed by rodent-borne orthohantaviruses, which cause severe, highly fatal human diseases worldwide.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population.
analysis.methods: Here, we implement an integrated ecological and machine learning framework combining 89 unique virus-host associations across 61 reservoir species with mechanistic Force-of-Infection (FOI) modeling to project global spillover hazards under current and future climate scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5) for 2041–2060.
analysis.main_results: Despite this significant public health risk, macroecological synthesis linking environmental drivers to systemic shifts in hantavirus hazards has been lacking.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: While thermal and precipitation anomalies predominate the transmission dynamics of Old and New World lineages like Sin-Nombre virus and Thailand virus, distinct urban-centric Profiles emerge for Seoul virus and Mamore virus, driven explicitly by fine-scale anthropogenic landscape modifications.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Our maps provide a critical baseline for targeted global surveillance and highlight the urgent need to integrate spatial conservation planning with public health preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These results reveal that climate change will not simply intensify viral spillover uniformly but will fundamentally restructure it across varied climatic and human-dominated environments.

analysis.summary_en: The 2026 multi-country cruise ship outbreak of Andes virus highlights the unpredictable and globalized threat posed by rodent-borne orthohantaviruses, which cause severe, highly fatal human diseases worldwide. The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population. Here, we implement an integrated ecological and machine learning framework combining 89 unique virus-host associations across 61 reservoir species with mechanistic Force-of-Infection (FOI) modeling to project global spillover hazards under current and future climate scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5) for 2041–2060. Despite this significant public health risk, macroecological synthesis linking environmental drivers to systemic shifts in hantavirus hazards has been lacking. While thermal and precipitation anomalies predominate the transmission dynamics of Old and New World lineages like Sin-Nombre virus and Thailand virus, distinct urban-centric Profiles emerge for Seoul virus and Mamore virus, driven explicitly by fine-scale anthropogenic landscape modifications. Our maps provide a critical baseline for targeted global surveillance and highlight the urgent need to integrate spatial conservation planning with public health preparedness. These results reveal that climate change will not simply intensify viral spillover uniformly but will fundamentally restructure it across varied climatic and human-dominated environments.

analysis.summary_en: While clinical features have been described in multiple studies, no previous systematic review has synthesised evidence on haemostatic dysfunction in HFRS. Observational studies and case series meeting predefined inclusion criteria were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools and, for one before-after cohort study, the National Institutes of Health (NIH) quality assessment tool. Thrombocytopenia was the most consistent abnormality, typically more pronounced in infections with Hantaan (HTNV), Dobrava (DOBV), and Seoul (SEOV) viruses compared with Puumala (PUUV), which was associated with milder disease. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: This review provides the first systematic synthesis of haemostatic dysfunction in HFRS. Variable study quality and incomplete reporting limit firm conclusions, underscoring the need for standardised, prospective studies of coagulation and bleeding outcomes.

title: Hantavirus and Middle East Public Health Challenges: A Subject Review

analysis.scope_and_question: There are two major clinical syndromes associated with human infections: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) — mostly reported from Europe and Asia, and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) — mostly reported from the Americas.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Current data suggest that while human infections are rare, ecological conditions which could sustain hantavirus are present in several Middle Eastern countries, and therefore increased surveillance and research into interdisciplinary and One Health initiatives are needed.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is limited surveillance, underdiagnosis, and a large clinical overlap with other febrile illnesses all of which are important challenges in quantifying the regional burden of disease.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Creating closer ties between the medical, veterinary and environmental communities is crucial for early outbreak detection and prevention in the future.

analysis.summary_en: There are two major clinical syndromes associated with human infections: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) — mostly reported from Europe and Asia, and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) — mostly reported from the Americas. The Middle East has a relatively low incidence of hantavirus disease, but recent epidemiological studies have shown that the virus is circulating in several countries, including Türkiye and Iran. Current data suggest that while human infections are rare, ecological conditions which could sustain hantavirus are present in several Middle Eastern countries, and therefore increased surveillance and research into interdisciplinary and One Health initiatives are needed. There is limited surveillance, underdiagnosis, and a large clinical overlap with other febrile illnesses all of which are important challenges in quantifying the regional burden of disease. Creating closer ties between the medical, veterinary and environmental communities is crucial for early outbreak detection and prevention in the future.

title: Spatiotemporal correlation analysis between climate change and hantavirus outbreak in Argentina: Quantitative causal inference based on Google Earth Engine and Bayesian spatiotemporal regression

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) cases in Argentina rose to 101 in the 2025–2026 season, nearly doubling from the prior season, with a marked geographical shift from Patagonia to Buenos Aires and the northwest NOA region. The study sought to quantify the spatiotemporal correlation and causal pathways between climate anomalies and hantavirus outbreaks using advanced geospatial and statistical tools.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed confirmed HPS cases from 2020 to 2026 reported by Argentine health authorities and international organizations, extracting onset dates and geographic coordinates. Climate data were integrated via the Google Earth Engine platform using ERA5-Land and NOAA GSOD datasets.
analysis.methods: Monthly climate anomalies (temperature, precipitation, soil moisture) and extreme weather frequencies were calculated using ERA5-Land and NOAA GSOD data accessed through Google Earth Engine. A Bayesian spatiotemporal Poisson regression with INLA estimated lag effects (1–6 months) and spatial heterogeneity, while causal mediation analysis identified the pathway from climate anomalies to human exposure via vegetation productivity and rodent population expansion.
analysis.main_results: The 2025–2026 HPS cases showed unstable spatial distribution (Moran's I = 0.42, p < 0.05), with outbreaks in NOA linked to drought-flood compound events following persistent drought. Vegetation index (NDVI) mediated 41.2% of the climate–HPS risk in Buenos Aires and 56.7% in NOA.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that drought-flood compound climate events drive hantavirus outbreaks through a trophic cascade involving vegetation productivity and rodent population expansion, representing the first national-scale quantitative causal inference of this relationship in Argentina.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the development of a GEE-based real-time monitoring framework for an HPS Climate-Driven Early Warning System in Argentina, enabling proactive public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on ecological associations and modeled climate data, which may not fully capture local transmission dynamics or unmeasured confounders, limiting causal inference strength to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the spatiotemporal link between climate anomalies and hantavirus outbreaks in Argentina during 2020–2026, focusing on the 2025–2026 epidemic season when cases nearly doubled and shifted geographically from Patagonia to Buenos Aires and the NOA region. Using Google Earth Engine, ERA5-Land and NOAA GSOD data were integrated to compute monthly climate anomalies and extreme weather frequencies. A Bayesian spatiotemporal Poisson regression with INLA estimated lagged and spatially heterogeneous effects of climate factors on HPS onset, while causal mediation analysis quantified the pathway from climate anomalies to human exposure via vegetation productivity and rodent population expansion. The 2025–2026 HPS cases exhibited unstable spatial clustering, and outbreaks in NOA were associated with drought-flood compound events following prolonged drought. Vegetation index mediated a substantial proportion of climate–HPS risk in Buenos Aires (41.2%) and NOA (56.7%). The authors interpret these findings as evidence that compound climate events drive outbreaks through ecological cascades, marking the first national-scale quantitative causal inference of this relationship. The study proposes a GEE-based early warning system to guide public health responses.

This study formulates and analyses a deterministic compartmental model for hantavirus transmission involving susceptible and infected rodents, susceptible, exposed, infectious and recovered humans, and an environmental viral reservoir.
